sections.title: What drives computer vision development cost
sections.description: The five factors that determine CV development cost.

blocks.heading: Driver 1: Task Complexity and Architecture
paragraphs: Binary image classification: $40,000–$70,000. Fine-tuned ResNet or EfficientNet with transfer learning achieves high accuracy with minimal labeled data.
Object detection: $50,000–$120,000. Requires detection architectures (YOLO, RT-DETR, DETR), more labeled training data, and more complex serving infrastructure.
Instance segmentation: $60,000–$140,000. More complex architectures (Mask R-CNN, SAM), more expensive annotation (polygon vs. bounding box), and larger model sizes.
Medical imaging AI: $70,000–$250,000. DICOM processing, clinical annotation, clinical validation study, FDA SaMD regulatory pathway.

blocks.heading: Driver 2: Data Labeling Requirements and Cost
paragraphs: Label type and cost per image: Binary classification: $0.05–$0.20. Multi-class classification: $0.10–$0.50. Bounding box: $0.50–$2.00 per object. Polygon/segmentation: $2.00–$8.00 per object. 3D bounding box: $5.00–$25.00 per frame. Medical imaging annotation: $10.00–$100.00 per image.

Label volume requirements (with transfer learning): Binary classification: 500–3,000 images per class. Multi-class: 300–2,000 per class. Object detection: 500–5,000 annotated images. Instance segmentation: 1,000–10,000. Medical imaging: 1,000–50,000.
Example labeling budget: 3,000 defect images × $0.80 = $2,400 + 3,000 defect-free images × $0.05 = $150. Total: ~$2,550. With 5 defect types on 8,000 total images: ~$12,000.
Labeling cost is included in ClickMasters' total project estimates — not disclosed as a separate line item.

blocks.heading: Driver 3: Active Learning vs. Random Sampling
paragraphs: Active learning typically reduces total labeling requirements by 30–60% compared to random sampling. For a project requiring 10,000 labeled images with random sampling, active learning might achieve equivalent accuracy with 4,000–7,000 labeled images.
ClickMasters implements active learning loops for all CV engagements where labeling is a significant cost driver.

blocks.heading: Driver 4: Deployment Environment
paragraphs: Cloud inference: Infrastructure cost addition: $5,000–$15,000. No model size constraints, auto-scaling.
On-premise server with GPU: Infrastructure cost addition: $8,000–$20,000. No data leaves the facility.
Edge GPU (NVIDIA Jetson): Infrastructure cost addition: $15,000–$35,000. Requires TensorRT quantization, pruning, OTA update infrastructure.
Mobile (iOS/Android): Infrastructure cost addition: $10,000–$25,000. Requires INT8/INT4 quantization, CoreML/TFLite optimization.

blocks.heading: Driver 5: Inference Speed Requirements
paragraphs: Batch processing (minutes to hours acceptable): Lowest infrastructure cost.
Near-real-time (1–10 seconds): Standard REST API serving, moderate cost.
Real-time (< 100ms): GPU-accelerated inference with TensorRT, highest cost.
Ultra-low-latency (< 10ms): Embedded GPU (Jetson) with TensorRT quantization.
Real-time and ultra-low-latency requirements add $15,000–$40,000 to base CV development cost.

blocks.heading: Industrial Quality Inspection CV
paragraphs: Binary pass/fail classifier: $45,000–$65,000. Multi-class defect classification: $55,000–$85,000. Edge GPU deployment (NVIDIA Jetson): add $20,000–$30,000. MES integration: add $8,000–$15,000. Total: $73,000–$130,000.

ROI: For a manufacturer with 0.5% defect rate generating $50 average warranty cost per escaped defect, 1M parts/year with 98% detection rate: 5,000 defects × $50 = $250,000 annual warranty cost avoided. Payback on $100,000 CV system: under 6 months.

blocks.heading: Medical Imaging AI
paragraphs: Chest X-ray pneumonia detection system: Clinical annotation (1,000 radiologist-annotated CXR): ~$30,000. Model development: $35,000–$50,000. Clinical validation study design: $15,000–$25,000. FDA SaMD advisory: $10,000–$20,000. DICOM infrastructure and PACS integration: $15,000–$30,000. Total: $105,000–$155,000.

blocks.heading: Retail Computer Vision (Loss Prevention)
paragraphs: Video analytics model for item mis-scanning detection: $55,000–$80,000. Multi-camera integration: add $15,000–$30,000. POS integration: add $8,000–$15,000. Total per store installation: $78,000–$125,000.
For a 200-store retailer with average $150,000 in self-checkout shrink per store, a 30% shrink reduction saves $9M annually. Payback: 27 months on full chain. Individual store payback: 8 months.

items.question: How much does computer vision development cost in 2026?
items.answer: CV development costs $40,000–$250,000+ depending on task type, data requirements, deployment environment, and compliance. Binary classification starts at $40,000. Object detection starts at $50,000. Medical imaging AI starts at $70,000. Full pricing above by CV type and cost driver.

items.question: What is the biggest hidden cost in computer vision development?
items.answer: Data labeling — consistently. Most CV cost estimates don't include labeling, or dramatically underestimate it. ClickMasters includes labeling cost in every project estimate, with a specific labeling plan (tool, annotator qualification, quality verification) as part of the Discovery deliverable.

items.question: How much does it cost to deploy CV on edge hardware (NVIDIA Jetson)?
items.answer: Edge deployment on NVIDIA Jetson (AGX Orin, TX2, or Nano) adds $15,000–$35,000 to base CV development cost for: TensorRT model optimization, edge deployment tooling, OTA update infrastructure, and production edge hardware configuration. The higher cost reflects the optimization work required to achieve production-line inference speeds on embedded hardware.

items.question: Can you achieve high accuracy with small labeled datasets?
items.answer: Yes. Transfer learning from foundation models (DINOv2, SAM, CLIP) achieves production-quality accuracy with 500–3,000 labeled images for classification and 500–5,000 for detection — 5–10× less data than training from scratch. Active learning further reduces labeling requirements by 30–60%. ClickMasters routinely achieves 95%+ accuracy on industrial CV tasks with under 5,000 labeled examples.

items.question: What does FDA SaMD advisory add to medical imaging AI cost?
items.answer: FDA SaMD advisory from ClickMasters costs $10,000–$20,000 and covers: SaMD classification determination, intended use documentation, clinical validation study design, substantial equivalence assessment for 510(k) pathway, and pre-submission meeting preparation. The clinical validation study itself is a separate cost ($50,000–$200,000+) that ClickMasters can scope and support.

items.question: How long does computer vision development take?
items.answer: Classification: 10–16 weeks. Object detection: 12–20 weeks. Medical imaging AI: 16–32 weeks. Edge deployment adds 3–6 weeks for optimization. Timeline is contractually binding from Discovery.
